written_by: Darby, award-level creative and UX pass 2026-10-04 evening (earlier version by worker e4475a)
person_made_it: Someone who knows Fina's is passed around by text and Instagram, so they took the board's own rules (cream ground, ink rules, protein colors) into Canva, then replaced Canva's invented food with the site's photos and fixed the address typo before anything shipped.
emcee_who_is_speaking: The host, one sentence about Fina and how to reach the kitchen.
what_time_of_day_is_this_room: Friday morning when the new board goes up, and Thursday afternoon before the 11:59 PM close; each graphic says which.
did_the_click_pay_me: Yes: one tap downloads a ready to post graphic at full size, and the caption sits next to it ready to paste.
works_for_the_recipient: Fina or Brian can post the week in under a minute without opening Canva; Gordon can still edit both designs in Canva.
taught_me_something: Canva's generator invents its own food photos even when given URLs; the site's photos had to be imported and placed by hand.
told_me_the_truth: Both graphics and the page say illustrative photos and sample prices; no prices, address or founder story appear.
weakest: The Thursday story's tall photo cells show the middle slice of each dish rather than whole containers, and the graphics are not yet posted anywhere; Fina posts them.
